# VULCAN Maintenance Report
**Asset:** HSM.F1.GBX01 | **Scenario:** SCN-038 | **Generated:** 2026-06-11
**Classification:** 🔴 HIGH RISK — IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED

---

## 1. DIAGNOSIS

Failure mode: **gear_tooth_fatigue_crack** [1]. Chunky spall debris confirmed in gearbox oil circuit [4]. Oil viscosity sensor JSR.HR.STD1.GBX01.OIL.VISC reading **216.601 cSt** is in WARNING band (warn threshold 180, alarm 265) [2].

> ⚠️ **Sensor/ML divergence noted:** ML fault classifier returns NORMAL (P=0.9999) [2], and anomaly score is sub-threshold at 0.4898 [3]. However, oil viscosity elevation + confirmed spall debris + prior cobble event constitute a hard clinical signal that overrides the classifier output. Safety class P2 — no deferral permitted [8].

---

## 2. ROOT CAUSE

Tooth-root fatigue crack initiated by a prior **high-torque cobble event** [1][4]. Cobble-induced torque spike exceeded tooth-root endurance limit (per AGMA 2101-D04 framework [7]), propagating a fatigue crack that has now generated chunky spall debris contaminating the oil circuit [4]. Cobble events are the primary tooth fatigue initiator on this asset class [9].

---

## 3. REMAINING USEFUL LIFE

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Estimated RUL | **632 cycles (~26.3 days)** [3] |
| RUL Band | Monitor [3][5] |
| Anomaly Score | 0.4898 — below anomaly threshold [3] |

**Operational interpretation:** RUL model has not flagged imminent failure, but this estimate was generated prior to confirmed spall debris classification. With a fatigue crack and active debris generation, the RUL trajectory is **not reliable for deferral decisions**. SOP-02 explicitly states this is an immediate-stop event once spall is confirmed [8].

---

## 4. RISK ASSESSMENT

**Risk Level: 🔴 HIGH — Score: 7/10** [5]

| Factor | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Process criticality (Criticality-1 asset) | +3 [5] |
| Safety class P2 | +2 [5] |
| P(failure) from ML = 0.00 | +0 [5] |
| RUL band = monitor | +0 [5] |
| Key spare GEAR-WHL-M20 out of stock, 36-week lead | +2 [5] |

The spare-stock situation is the critical compounding factor. A fracture event without the spare in hand results in **168 hours unplanned downtime** [1] with no workaround path.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDED ACTIONS

Execute **Option B — Major Overhaul** per SOP-02 [6][7]:

1. **Immediate controlled stop — no deferral** [4][6][8]
2. Remove gearbox via crane to repair bay [4][6]
3. Inspect all gear teeth under workshop lighting; classify damage per AGMA 2101-D04 (pitting, spalling, micro-pitting, scuffing, tooth-root fracture); photograph every tooth from reference mark [10]
4. Remove damaged gear wheel using hydraulic press; if shrink-fit, apply localised induction heat to gear boss only — **no direct flame** (risk of shaft annealing) [10]
5. Inspect gear seat on shaft for fretting/wear; measure against OEM tolerance — if worn, machine-shop regrind and chrome-spray required [10]
6. Replace gear wheel + full bearing set [4][6]
7. Set backlash **0.1–0.3 mm** — measure with dial gauge at minimum 8 positions around circumference [4][11]
8. Verify gear tooth contact with Prussian-blue compound: contact must be centred and cover **>70% face width and >60% tooth height** [4][11]
9. Run-in at low load before returning to full mill drive [4][6]

---

## 6. SPARE PROCUREMENT

| Action | Part | Description | Status | Lead Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 **ORDER NOW** | GEAR-WHL-M20 | Custom large-module gear wheel M20+ (HSM mill drive) | **Out of stock** | **36 weeks** — Flender/Renk OEM [6] |
| ✅ Issue from store | BRG-GBX-SET | Full bearing set | 1 unit on hand | Immediate [6] |

> **Critical procurement note:** 36-week lead on GEAR-WHL-M20 means the order must be raised **today** to have the spare available before the next credible fracture window [6][9]. Per SOP-02, procurement should have been triggered the moment ferrous particles first trended above 5 ppm [9].

**Total parts cost: ₹1,03,95,750 (INR)** [6]

| Unplanned downtime (if fracture) | **168 hours (~7 days)** [1] |
| Estimated production loss | **₹5,01,00,000 / USD 600,000** [1] |
| Cost range (7-day swap, secondary damage) | **USD 500,000 – 3,000,000** [1] |
| Parts cost | **₹1,03,95,750** [6] |

The USD 600k point estimate reflects a ~7-day swap of the custom large-module gear wheel plus secondary-damage repair [1]. Risk of escalation to the USD 3M ceiling exists if secondary damage to pinion or shaft is found during teardown [1].

---

## 8. RECURRENCE PREVENTION

- Monthly ferrographic oil analysis — mandatory; detects spall particles **2–4 weeks before GMF alarm escalation** [9]
- Implement continuous kidney-loop filtration targeting ISO 4406 < 16/14/11 [9]
- Connect torque measurement to CMMS; auto-raise work order if torque exceeds **110% rated for >5 seconds** to capture future cobble events at source [9]
- Enforce full run-in procedure after every gear replacement [9]
